sources.title: HarmonyOS Engineering domain manifest
claims: The registered Domain is engineering.harmonyos, named HarmonyOS Engineering.
Its purpose is reusable HarmonyOS application delivery practice and evaluation.
Its owner is platform-harmony, version is 0.1.0, and lifecycle is draft.

sources.title: Introduction to ArkTS
claims: ArkTS is the HarmonyOS application language based on TypeScript and applies stricter static typing and restrictions to dynamic features.
ArkTS language, module, type, interoperability, and concurrency rules are implementation-correctness concerns.

sources.title: Stage Model Development Guide
claims: The Stage model defines HarmonyOS application components, lifecycle, context, process, thread, configuration, and ArkUI page integration.
UIAbility handles user-facing application components while ExtensionAbility derivatives serve system-defined extension scenarios.

sources.title: ObservedV2 and Trace: Observing Class Property Changes
claims: ObservedV2 and Trace, supported from API version 12, work together to observe selected class properties including nested objects.
Untraced properties do not trigger UI refresh, and V1 and V2 decorators have documented mixing restrictions.

sources.title: Migrating Data Object State Variables from ArkUI State Management V1 to V2
claims: Migration maps ObjectLink, Observed, and Track scenarios to ObservedV2 and Trace with scenario-specific changes.
V2 supports direct nested-property observation and precise updates, so migration is behavioral rather than token-only replacement.

sources.title: HarmonyOS Application Package Glossary
claims: App is the publication unit, HAP is an installation and runtime unit, HAR is a static shared package, and HSP is a runtime shared package.
Package selection determines module delivery and code or resource reuse behavior.

sources.title: Getting Started with HarmonyOS Developer Testing Services
claims: HarmonyOS verification includes configurable Code Linter checks, unit tests, coverage analysis, and application or atomic-service self-inspection.
Verification can produce evidence for correctness, compatibility, performance, power, security, stability, and functionality.

capability_hypotheses.description: Retrieve version-relevant ArkTS, ArkUI, SDK, API, and migration documentation and return traceable evidence before advising or coding.
Implement and review ArkTS code under documented typing, syntax, module, interoperability, and concurrency constraints.
Design, implement, and evaluate declarative ArkUI screens, interactions, navigation, and state-driven rendering within the selected API baseline.
Plan and verify scenario-specific ArkUI state-management V1-to-V2 migration, including nested observation and decorator compatibility.
Detect deprecated or incompatible SDK usage, identify documented replacements, and verify migrations instead of applying unreviewed substitutions.
Design and review Stage-model application structure, UIAbility lifecycle, context use, extension boundaries, and execution concerns.
Select HAP, HAR, and HSP boundaries according to installation, publication, and reuse requirements.
Produce reproducible lint, build, test, coverage, package, and device-facing verification evidence for HarmonyOS delivery.
